title: Ethics and Metaphysics for Everyone
subtitle: What you should do, and whether any of it is real
series_title: A Standalone Popular-Philosophy Companion to Physics Won't Hurt You
based_on: the documented history of ethical and metaphysical philosophy, plus an honest, clearly-flagged tour of live open questions and speculative frontiers (personal identity, free will, the hard problem of consciousness, the simulation argument, the moral status of machines) — ORIGINAL SYNTHESIS in the author's own words, not a derivative of any single existing popular-philosophy book
author: Andries J. Greyling
protagonist: an ensemble cast of philosophers across twenty-five centuries, narrated by the same warm, funny, plain-spoken authorial voice as Physics Won't Hurt You (Bryson/Sapiens register)
setting: Athens to Konigsberg to Oxford to a laboratory timing the exact moment a decision happens, c. 400 BCE-present
logline: Physics told you what's true. This is the book about what you're supposed to do about it, and whether 'you' is even the right word for the thing doing the deciding — the two oldest, least cooperative arguments in philosophy, told with the same curiosity and honesty their older sibling gave to physics.
blueprint: five-part survey plus a closing chapter: (I) What Should I Do? - normative ethics from Socrates to Rawls; (II) Am I Even Real? - personal identity, determinism, free will, consciousness; (III) Is Anything Real? - metaphysics of the external world, from Plato's cave to the simulation argument; (IV) Where the Two Arguments Meet - the moral status of machines and animals, effective altruism; (V) The Same Questions, Asked Elsewhere - Egyptian ma'at, African relational personhood/ubuntu, Buddhist anatta and emptiness, Confucian virtue, Stoicism, each read directly against its Western counterpart earlier in the book; closing chapter ties back to Physics Won't Hurt You's own thesis, applied to values instead of facts, now with a global cast.
market: readers of Bill Bryson's A Short History of Nearly Everything, Yuval Noah Harari's Sapiens, Michael Sandel's Justice, Rebecca Goldstein, and Derek Parfit's popularizers
status: DRAFT COMPLETE (24 ch across 5 parts + front/backmatter, ~25k, full send, EPUB rebuilt after every finished chapter, 2026-08-30) - Part Five folded in from MAXIMAL_ATLAS.md quarry doc, remainder of that atlas reserved for a possible future expanded edition
tone: warm, funny, plain-spoken, unafraid of the strange; identical register to Physics Won't Hurt You - honest about what's a live philosophical consensus (in the loose sense the field allows), a genuinely open debate, or a minority/speculative position, never letting a tidy story overstate how settled any of it is
dedication: For everyone who ever asked a grown-up what they were supposed to do, got an answer that didn't quite hold up, and kept asking anyway. And for Yuval Noah Harari, whose Sapiens freed this author's mind long before this book existed, and without which it would not exist in its present shape either. Thank you. And for Bill Bryson, whose A Short History of Nearly Everything taught this author that a hard idea could be handed to a total stranger as a gift instead of a homework assignment, and that a footnote could be funnier than the chapter it was attached to. Thank you.
clearances: All historical figures depicted are deceased and long-documented public figures of major historical record (Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, Kant, Bentham, Mill, Berkeley, Hume, Rawls, Libet, Confucius, Mencius, Xunzi, Epictetus, Marcus Aurelius, Nagarjuna, Ptahhotep, Desmond Tutu, John Mbiti, Kwame Gyekye, Ifeanyi Menkiti, et al.) -> depictable. Living philosophers referenced (e.g. Derek Parfit's intellectual heirs, contemporary trolleyology researchers, living scholars cited for the Menkiti-Gyekye debate) are discussed only via their documented, published academic work, never fictionalized in scene. This is an ORIGINAL narrative synthesis; no sentence is copied from any existing popular-philosophy book (Sandel, Goldstein, Blackburn, or any philosopher's own writing), nor from MAXIMAL_ATLAS.md itself, which was consulted only for its structural ideas and source names, never for prose.
sensitivity_read: not required - historical/philosophical record and documented academic debate, no living-person exposure beyond citation of public published work.
